title: PR gating: statistical drift detector for CI benchmarking
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: add a robust statistical drift detector into the CI perf harness so PRs that introduce regressions in tokens/sec (and other latency/throughput signals) are automatically flagged or blocked. This ticket covers: (1) lightweight per-PR perf runs with calibrated sampling, (2) comparison against historical baselines using non-parametric tests and control charts, and (3) deterministic gating logic that balances sensitivity vs. flakiness.

Background: current PR perf checks are noisy — single-run p95s vary with runner noise, model warmup, and trace sampling. We need a principled detector that: (a) preserves low false-positive rate for small noise-induced shifts, (b) catches medium-to-large regressions quickly (10%+ p95 degradation), and (c) integrates into GitHub Actions / Linear rollouts.

Approach:
- Baselines: maintain rolling window distributions per model/config/hardware (model name, quantization profile, sequence length bucket, GPU type). Store HDR histograms + sample summaries in object storage with metadata fingerprints.
- PR-run protocol: run 3 independent shards (separate VM warmups) each executing N short measured runs (default N=50 tokens/sec samples for the target seq_len distribution). Use the same tokenization and cached KV warmup sequence as production trace sampling. Use deterministic seeds for synthetic inputs where appropriate to reduce variance.
- Metrics: tokens/sec (throughput), p95 latency (per-token or per-chunk), median, interquartile range, and a small set of secondary signals (CPU steal, GPU SM utilization, mem bandwidth).
- Statistical tests & detection: use a two-stage detector: (1) distributional shift test (KS test / Mann-Whitney U) comparing PR sample pool to baseline distribution (p-value threshold configurable, default 0.005); (2) effect-size threshold on p95 / median (default block if p95 degrades >10% and effect size Cohen's d > 0.35). Complement tests with an EWMA control chart for trend detection to catch gradual regressions.
- Flake protection: require detection in >=2 independent shards OR repeated failures across two CI runs within 24 hours to block. Provide advisory warnings for single-run anomalies instead of hard blocking.
- Results reporting: attach per-PR summary artifact (JSON + HDR hist) and link to perf dashboard with deterministic diff visualization (sample distributions, ECDF, control chart). Add human-readable explanation and remediation tips (e.g., point to likely causes: batching changes, kernel selection, KV cache warming changes).

Integration plan: GitHub Action runs the harness on PR label `perf-check`. The runner will upload artifacts to s3://redwood-ci-perf/ENG-17645/<pr-number>/<timestamp>. A lightweight gating service evaluates the detector and posts a comment/action status back to GitHub and to the PR build. The service also writes a short event to the perf dashboard for triage.

Acceptance criteria:
- Detector runs in <= 12 minutes for the default small benchmark matrix (3 shards x N=50) and <= 90s added scheduling overhead.
- False positive rate on historical CI traces <= 2% (measured over last 90 days).
- Blocks PR when p95 tokens/sec regression is >= 10% with statistical significance and shard agreement.
- PR artifact schema published and dashboard integration validated.

Out of scope: full rollout to nightly full-matrix benchmarks (separate ticket), automatic rollback orchestration, and dedicated on-prem runner tuning (follow-ups planned).
comments: 2026-03-10 - Ava Martinez: Created ticket after incident on 2026-03-08 where a merged change regressed p95 by ~18% and slipped through due to noisy single-run gating. Initial design doc sketched (see links).

2026-03-11 - Devon Patel: Completed prototype harness that runs 3 shards x 30 samples. Early local runs show standard deviation on p95 ~3% for stable commits. Pushed prototype branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4128.

2026-03-12 - Priya Singh (runtime): Reviewed detector logic. Suggested tightening p-value to 0.002 for GPUs with known runner variability and adding EWMA smoothing to avoid one-off spikes. Also flagged potential cost impact of increasing sample counts.

2026-03-12 - QA: Ran historical replay (200 PRs) against prototype. Detector flagged 9 regressions; 7 were true positives (confirmed by manual trace and perf flamegraphs), 2 were flaky. Preparing a follow-up to tune shard agreement rule.

2026-03-13 - Devon Patel: Updated prototype to store HDR histograms and JSON summary. Dashboard ingestion endpoint POST /perf/ci/ingest added in service branch. Open item: consolidate fingerprinting logic with existing baseline service (ENG-17001).
notes: Planned rollout: alpha to runtime and infra teams for two cycles, then set policy to advisory, then mandatory block on P0 repos. Cost modelling suggests ~30-40% increase in CI time for perf-check labeled PRs until we add smarter sampling.
